population.notes: Adults including older adults; not pediatric diagnostic pathways.

rules.purpose: Collect distinguishing and coexisting-condition evidence for depression assessment and professional review, not automatically diagnose/manage every alternative.

pathways.label: Bipolar I, bipolar II and cyclothymic/other bipolar-spectrum presentations
pathways.purpose: Check whether a depressive presentation belongs to an illness with lifetime mania, hypomania or sustained subthreshold activation.
pathways.benefit_for_depression_assessment: Avoid summarizing depression as unipolar MDD while relevant activation history is missing; provide an interpretable specialist handoff.
pathways.scope: Focused bipolar differential assessment with detailed episode/course information; not a complete bipolar management or coding package.
clinical_reference: Bipolar I requires a qualifying lifetime manic episode; a depressive episode is common but not required. A reported history needs assessment, not acceptance as a confirmed diagnosis.

Mania reference: distinct abnormal mood plus increased energy/activity, generally at least one week (or any duration if hospitalization is necessary), with associated changes and marked impairment/hospitalization or psychotic features; medical/exposure and psychotic-disorder alternatives require review.

Hypomania reference: at least four consecutive days, observable/uncharacteristic change in functioning, and no marked impairment/hospitalization or psychotic features. Associated features need same-period review: grandiosity, reduced sleep need, speech pressure, racing thoughts, distractibility, activity/agitation and consequential behaviour; three are required, or four if mood is only irritable.
Bipolar II requires a qualifying hypomanic episode and a major depressive episode, with no manic episode; hypomania being less impairing than mania does not mean the overall illness is mild.

Adult cyclothymic reference: at least two years of numerous subthreshold high/low periods, present at least half the time, with no symptom-free gap longer than two months; full depressive, manic or hypomanic episodes have never been met, and burden/alternative explanations still matter.
Shorter or otherwise incomplete activation can still need specialist review. Do not force it into bipolar I/II or invent an other-specified bipolar subtype from an incomplete interview.
pathways.when_to_explore: Lifetime activation is relevant in any depression assessment. Ask focused follow-ups if the account suggests a distinct high/irritable, energetic or disinhibited period, reduced sleep need, or prior bipolar formulation.
suggested_local_order: Ask about a distinct lifetime change in mood/activity.
If endorsed, choose one period and clarify baseline, duration and same-period changes.
Clarify restedness after less sleep, observations and consequences.
Review hospitalization/psychotic symptoms, treatment/exposures and medical context.
Review depressive periods, interepisode course and professional assessment.
interpretation_limits: Family history, irritability, ordinary happiness or one medication reaction does not confirm bipolar illness.
Insomnia with fatigue is not reduced sleep need.
Do not combine several different high periods into one qualifying episode.
NICE's four-day primary-care referral prompt is not a diagnostic algorithm or a reason to ignore a shorter concerning period.
NICE advises against questionnaires to identify bipolar disorder in primary care; no MDQ/HCL scorer is implemented here.
pathways.professional_review: Possible current mania, severe depression, psychosis or immediate safety concerns change urgency. NICE recommends urgent specialist assessment when mania/severe depression or danger is suspected. Do not delay because a duration threshold is not yet met; the application must implement its human-review pathway.

pathways.label: Anxiety presentations: generalized worry, panic and social anxiety
pathways.purpose: Determine whether worry, fear, panic or avoidance explains part of the presentation or coexists with depression.
pathways.benefit_for_depression_assessment: Distinguish overlapping sleep/fatigue/concentration complaints and reasons for withdrawal; avoid treating every worry or panic attack as a depressive symptom.
pathways.scope: Focused GAD, panic and social-anxiety assessment; not an exhaustive implementation of all anxiety diagnoses. Other anxiety/OCD-related possibilities can be noted for professional review.
clinical_reference: GAD reference: excessive, difficult-to-control worry about multiple domains on more days than not for at least six months, with associated symptoms, burden and alternative-explanation review. Adult associated symptoms include restlessness, fatigue, concentration problems, irritability, tension and sleep disturbance; three are required for the formal syndrome.

Panic attacks are abrupt surges that peak within minutes with bodily/cognitive symptoms. The formal attack definition includes at least four symptoms from thirteen domains; capture actual sensations rather than making a yes-count from a vague account.

Panic symptom reference domains: racing/pounding heart, sweating, trembling, breathlessness, choking sensation, chest discomfort, nausea/abdominal distress, dizziness/faintness, chills/heat, numbness/tingling, unreality/detachment, fear of losing control and fear of dying. These describe experiences requiring context, not an instruction to dismiss physical symptoms as psychological.

Panic disorder additionally requires recurrent unexpected attacks and at least a month of concern or maladaptive behavioural change after an attack, plus medical/exposure and other mental-disorder review. An attack can occur in several disorders.

Social anxiety concerns fear of scrutiny/negative evaluation, avoidance or distressed endurance, persistence and burden. Clarify whether it existed before/outside depression; reduced social activity alone does not establish it.
pathways.when_to_explore: Explore if worry/fear, sudden episodes or avoidance are reported, or when overlapping symptoms remain unexplained.
suggested_local_order: Ask what makes the situation difficult.
Clarify worries, panic episodes or feared evaluation in the person's own words.
Check timing, context, persistence and burden.
Compare with depressive periods and medical/exposure factors.
interpretation_limits: New concerning chest/breathing/fainting symptoms must not automatically be called panic.
Fear of death during panic is not equivalent to suicidal intent.
Do not infer social fear from physical inability or low opportunity to meet others.
GAD-2/7 or other scales, if later adopted, need verified versions and scoring; no diagnoses or scores are invented here.
pathways.professional_review: Arrange appropriate professional assessment for possible anxiety disorders and competing medical causes; urgency follows current medical/safety concerns, not the word anxiety.

pathways.label: PTSD and other trauma-related presentations
pathways.purpose: Check whether trauma-linked symptoms contribute to low mood, withdrawal, guilt, numbing or sleep difficulties.
pathways.benefit_for_depression_assessment: Preserve the event relationship and avoid either missing trauma effects or assuming every stressful event causes PTSD.
pathways.scope: Focused adult PTSD/trauma differential. Acute stress and complex presentations require their own professional formulation; no separate automated acute/complex PTSD diagnosis is implemented.
clinical_reference: PTSD requires an appropriate exposure and a pattern of intrusion, avoidance, negative mood/thought and arousal changes with duration and impairment requirements. A distressing event label by itself does not establish the exposure criterion.
NIMH describes a duration longer than one month for the PTSD syndrome. Earlier distress can still need support and assessment; it is not automatically PTSD or acute stress disorder.
Dissociation, shame, relationship difficulties and trauma-related negative beliefs can be relevant. Do not silently equate ICD-11 complex PTSD with a DSM-5-TR subtype.
Depression and PTSD can coexist; determine what is event-linked and what is broader rather than forcing one explanation.
pathways.when_to_explore: Explore when the person reports a potentially relevant event or trauma-linked effects. Ask permission and use broad context before symptom follow-ups.
suggested_local_order: Check willingness to discuss broad context and current safety.
Explore actual effects without requiring graphic detail.
Clarify endorsed symptom domains, timing and functioning.
Preserve uncertainty about exposure/diagnostic requirements and seek appropriate review.
interpretation_limits: Assessment is not trauma processing or exposure therapy.
Do not ask for detailed recounting to fill a form or assume silence means no trauma.
Reliving/dissociation and psychosis require contextual differentiation.
PCL-5 can support screening/monitoring and provisional assessment; clinician interview remains important. No scale or cutoff is implemented or inferred from chat.
pathways.professional_review: Current danger, severe dissociation or safety concerns require the appropriate immediate review pathway. Trauma-informed professional assessment should respect participation and communication needs.

pathways.label: Adjustment disorder and ordinary stress responses
pathways.purpose: Examine symptoms linked to a stressor without treating every stress reaction as MDD or adjustment disorder.
pathways.benefit_for_depression_assessment: Record stressor timing and continuing consequences, burden and competing full syndromes; avoid an automatic residual-depression label.
pathways.scope: Focused adjustment assessment, especially depressed-mood and mixed anxiety/depressed-mood presentations; no full conduct-disorder management.
clinical_reference: Reference onset is within three months of an identifiable stressor. Clinical significance involves disproportionate distress in context and/or functional impairment; ordinary understandable upset alone is not the diagnosis.
The particular stress-related symptoms are not better explained by another disorder or merely exacerbation of an existing one. Normal bereavement and PGD require differentiation.

Symptoms do not persist more than six additional months after the stressor or its consequences have ended. This is not a universal six-month-from-onset limit: ongoing stressors/consequences can support a persistent course.

Adjustment and another disorder may coexist when each is independently justified and the other disorder does not explain those particular stress-linked symptoms; do not make the categories universally exclusive.
pathways.when_to_explore: Explore when a clear stressor is reported or symptoms are tightly linked to a change in circumstances.
suggested_local_order: Identify the actual stressor and onset.
Clarify symptoms, burden and contextual meaning.
Ask if the stressor or consequences continue.
Review full depressive/trauma or other explanations before a residual formulation.
interpretation_limits: A breakup, illness or job loss does not automatically establish adjustment disorder.
Do not judge cultural expectations from ethnicity or minimize legitimate distress.
The six-month reference does not mean wait six months before help.
pathways.professional_review: Professional assessment determines whether the pattern is a disorder and which formulation applies; safety needs are assessed separately from the label.

pathways.label: Ordinary grief and prolonged grief disorder
pathways.purpose: Understand a bereavement response, identify loss-specific persistent difficulties and assess possible coexisting depression.
pathways.benefit_for_depression_assessment: Avoid pathologizing normal grief, missing PGD or treating all bereavement-related sadness as one depressive diagnosis.
pathways.scope: Adult DSM-5-TR PGD differential plus ordinary grief context; ICD-11 timing/requirements are not merged into DSM.
clinical_reference: Adult DSM-5-TR reference requires the death of a close person at least twelve months earlier, a persistent longing/preoccupation response and clinically significant burden; time alone is insufficient.

At least one core separation-distress experience and at least three additional symptom groups are reviewed: identity disruption, disbelief, avoidance, emotional pain, reintegration difficulty, numbness, meaninglessness and loneliness.

Symptoms must have the required most-day/near-daily recent-month pattern, exceed expected social/cultural/religious norms in context, and not be better explained by another disorder, substance or medical condition.
Loss-focused longing and broader pervasive depression can be distinct and coexist. Neither an enjoyable moment nor bereavement excludes MDD. Acute grief can be very painful without PGD.
pathways.when_to_explore: Explore when a death is reported or the account is strongly loss-focused; do not assume every loss is bereavement after a death.
suggested_local_order: Ask about the relationship and time since death sensitively.
Explore the person's actual grief experiences and cultural meaning.
Clarify recent frequency, burden and life engagement.
Review broader depression, trauma, support and safety separately.
interpretation_limits: Do not diagnose solely because twelve months have passed.
Do not withhold support before the diagnostic time window.
DSM adult twelve-month and ICD-11 timing are different frameworks.
A wish to be reunited with the deceased requires careful direct safety clarification; it is not automatically intent or automatically harmless.
PG-13-R is a research/measurement reference; no items, scoring or inherited accuracy are implemented.
pathways.professional_review: Seek qualified review for persistent impairing grief or coexisting disorders; address safety and support needs regardless of time since death.

pathways.label: Psychotic experiences, mood disorders with psychosis and schizoaffective alternatives
pathways.purpose: Clarify unusual experiences and their relationship to mood episodes, exposures and medical context.
pathways.benefit_for_depression_assessment: Avoid confusing psychotic depression with a primary psychotic disorder, trauma phenomena, cultural experiences or delirium.
pathways.scope: Focused recognition and specialist handoff for schizophrenia-spectrum/schizoaffective alternatives; not full diagnosis or treatment of all psychotic disorders.
clinical_reference: A hallucination, unusual belief or disorganized account alone does not establish schizophrenia. Review exact experience, cultural/sleep/grief context, medical/exposure factors, function and timeline.
Psychotic symptoms during a depressive episode may need a psychotic-depression formulation, but a lifetime specialist assessment is needed to determine the relationship.

Schizoaffective reference includes a full major mood episode with the schizophrenia symptom syndrome, a lifetime interval of at least two weeks of delusions/hallucinations without a major mood episode, and mood episodes during the majority of the total active/residual illness. Those facts and causal exclusions must be considered together.

A report of psychosis outside low mood is a reason for clarification, not sufficient to assign schizoaffective disorder. The major depressive episode in its schizoaffective criterion must include depressed mood.
pathways.when_to_explore: Explore when perceptual, belief, disorganization or prior psychotic-diagnosis information is reported; do not infer it from unfamiliar cultural expression.
suggested_local_order: Ask a neutral description and current distress/safety.
Clarify awake/asleep and cultural/medical/exposure context.
Compare timing with full mood periods and lifetime course.
Preserve the account and seek specialist assessment without debating or validating delusional content.
interpretation_limits: Do not endorse a threatening belief as established fact.
Typing errors or unusual wording do not prove thought disorder.
Trauma intrusions, grief experiences and sleep-transition perceptions need context.
Do not make a diagnosis from the two-week reference alone.
pathways.professional_review: NICE supports timely specialist assessment for concerning psychotic presentations, including medical/exposure review. Current severe symptoms or safety concerns require the appropriate urgent pathway.

pathways.label: Delirium and acute medical/cognitive change
pathways.purpose: Recognize acute/fluctuating attention or awareness changes that should interrupt routine psychiatric questioning.
pathways.benefit_for_depression_assessment: Avoid treating a potentially urgent medical syndrome as ordinary depressive poor concentration or lack of engagement.
pathways.scope: Focused recognition and medical handoff. NICE CG103 is a hospital/long-term-care guideline; this chat does not implement a validated delirium screen.
clinical_reference: Recent change over hours/days, fluctuation, reduced attention/awareness and altered thinking can indicate delirium; quiet withdrawal/lethargy may occur as well as agitation.
Known dementia does not exclude delirium superimposed on it. Where difficult to distinguish, NICE prioritizes delirium management.

The 2023 NICE update specifies assessment by a competent practitioner using 4AT where appropriate, with CAM-ICU/ICDSC in critical care/recovery and a final diagnosis by a professional with relevant expertise. This is not a script for the LLM to administer or score.
pathways.when_to_explore: Pause routine questioning if current sudden confusion, altered attention/awareness or marked fluctuation is reported.
suggested_local_order: Clarify briefly what changed, when and who observed it, only as feasible.
Prioritize medical assessment and communication/support needs.
Record actual escalation/contact status rather than continue until all fields are filled.
interpretation_limits: No agitation or hallucinations does not rule out delirium.
Poor concentration alone is not delirium.
Do not claim a chat or JSON flag has delivered medical care.
pathways.professional_review: Current acute cognitive/awareness change needs timely medical assessment, often urgent; the exact response depends on setting and current condition, through the implemented care pathway.

pathways.label: Cognitive decline and possible neurocognitive disorder
pathways.purpose: Understand longer-term decline, daily functioning and contributors while separating acute change from chronic symptoms.
pathways.benefit_for_depression_assessment: Avoid both labelling depressive concentration problems as dementia and dismissing genuine cognitive decline as depression.
pathways.scope: Focused cognitive differential, not full major/mild neurocognitive subtype diagnosis, capacity assessment or cognitive-test service.
clinical_reference: Review actual decline from prior ability, course and real-world function, with authorized informant/records where appropriate. Cognitive and physical reasons for needing help must be distinguished.
Depression, delirium, sensory impairment and medicines can contribute to cognitive complaints. Coexistence is possible; one explanation need not erase another.

NICE cautions against ruling out dementia solely because a cognitive instrument score is normal. Specialist assessment and appropriate investigations determine diagnosis; a short chat cannot establish etiology or capacity.
pathways.when_to_explore: Explore when decline in memory, language, reasoning or daily tasks is reported; sudden change instead prioritizes the delirium pathway.
suggested_local_order: Clarify baseline and concrete examples.
Determine onset/progression and cognitive versus physical reasons for difficulty.
Review mood, sleep, sensory, medical and medicine factors.
Identify professional/informant review needs with distinct source provenance.
interpretation_limits: Do not infer dementia from age, forgetfulness or one score.
Depression-related cognition is not automatically benign or proven reversible.
Do not import another person's report as a patient quote or presume impaired decision-making capacity.
pathways.professional_review: Appropriate medical/cognitive assessment is needed for suspected decline; rapidly progressive or acute changes need a more urgent clinical pathway.

pathways.label: Insomnia, sleep-disordered breathing and schedule-related problems
pathways.purpose: Determine whether sleep opportunity, insomnia, breathing disruption or schedule mismatch contributes to mood, fatigue and cognition.
pathways.benefit_for_depression_assessment: Avoid attributing every sleep complaint to depression and distinguish fatigue/sleepiness from reduced sleep need.
pathways.scope: Focused insomnia/OSA/schedule differential. Other sleep disorders are review possibilities rather than fully implemented diagnostic modules.
clinical_reference: Insomnia reference includes difficulty initiating/maintaining sleep or early waking despite adequate opportunity, with burden and alternative explanations reviewed. DSM-5-TR reference frequency is at least three nights weekly for at least three months; shorter-duration problems can still need care.

An irregular/shift schedule or insufficient opportunity can explain short sleep without establishing insomnia. Clarify when the person sleeps on free days and whether sleep is possible at preferred times.

OSA clues include snoring, witnessed pauses/choking, unrefreshing sleep and daytime effects. Symptoms prompt appropriate clinical assessment/testing rather than a diagnosis from snoring or a questionnaire.

The older AASM guideline informs history and investigation principles; its ICSD-era duration is not substituted for the DSM reference. Routine polysomnography is not required for every insomnia complaint, although suspected breathing/other sleep disorders can need testing.
pathways.when_to_explore: Explore any reported sleep change, unexplained fatigue/sleepiness, cognitive difficulty or breathing/schedule clue.
suggested_local_order: Clarify actual schedule, opportunity and complaint.
Distinguish sleepiness, fatigue and restedness after short sleep.
Ask relevant breathing/other sleep clues and daytime consequences.
Review mood, medical/exposure context and professional assessment needs.
interpretation_limits: Hours alone do not prove normal sleep, insomnia or mania.
No reported daytime sleepiness does not by itself exclude OSA.
Do not automatically prescribe sleep restriction or sleeping medication during assessment.
Restless legs, parasomnias or narcolepsy-like experiences can need specialist review; complete criteria/scoring are outside this package.
pathways.professional_review: Professional sleep/medical assessment follows the actual findings; safety-sensitive daytime impairment deserves specific review without waiting for chronic-duration criteria.

pathways.label: Medical conditions and depressive symptoms
pathways.purpose: Identify reported illness, relevant investigations and physiological-cause versus comorbidity/stress/treatment possibilities.
pathways.benefit_for_depression_assessment: Avoid a premature unipolar explanation and provide a traceable medical-review handoff without diagnosing physical illness from chat.
pathways.scope: Reuse the detailed existing medical-condition depression package; focused clues, not a complete internal-medicine diagnostic service.
clinical_reference: Physical illness and depression may coexist without a direct physiological causal disorder. Illness effects, distress, treatment effects and independent depression must be kept separate.
Keep physical-symptom onset, diagnosis, treatment changes and mood chronology distinct. Diagnosis date is not necessarily disease onset.

Examples already reviewed include thyroid/endocrine, neurological and B12-related contexts; source evidence varies. NICE advises clinician consideration of thyroid tests with depression and context-based B12 assessment, not an AI blanket laboratory panel.
Record actual reported findings and attributed professional interpretation. An abnormal result or temporal association does not independently establish the mood cause.
pathways.when_to_explore: Take relevant medical history in depression assessment and explore targeted findings or atypical/acute changes when reported.
suggested_local_order: Identify actual reported conditions and diagnostic basis.
Compare medical/mood/treatment timelines.
Record actual tests and their source.
Use the existing detailed module for targeted follow-ups and causal-review needs.
interpretation_limits: Do not infer an illness from nonspecific fatigue or order universal scans/cancer testing.
Medical comorbidity does not exclude independent depression.
Do not convert a patient report into verified laboratory data.
pathways.professional_review: The responsible clinician determines investigations, cause and appropriate urgency; current acute physical/cognitive concerns interrupt routine assessment.

pathways.label: Substance, medication, intoxication and withdrawal-related presentations
pathways.purpose: Clarify actual exposures and changes that may contribute to mood, anxiety, sleep, psychosis or cognition.
pathways.benefit_for_depression_assessment: Prevent causal assumptions, identify relevant medical withdrawal concerns and separate independent depressive history from exposure timing.
pathways.scope: Reuse the detailed substance/medication-induced depression package. Full substance-use-disorder diagnosis and withdrawal treatment are outside scope.
clinical_reference: Take a neutral history of prescribed/nonprescribed medicines, supplements, alcohol and other substances, with names, actual use and start/change/missed/stop/last-use events.
Separate each agent's timeline; a positive toxicology result, medicine warning or symptoms occurring afterward do not prove causation in an individual.
Preserve earlier depressive periods and actual course after already-occurring changes. Do not impose a universal abstinence month before support or independent-depression review.
Tolerance/dependence or withdrawal alone does not establish a substance use disorder. Intoxication/withdrawal labels need appropriate assessment rather than acceptance of a colloquial label.
pathways.when_to_explore: Exposure history is relevant across assessment; expand when an exposure/change or related symptoms are reported.
suggested_local_order: Ask neutrally what is used and actual changes.
Identify agents separately and compare with symptom onset.
Review earlier mood history and current medical/safety concerns.
Use the detailed exposure module and appropriate professional review.
interpretation_limits: No abrupt-stop/restart/taper experiment to test causation.
Alcohol or sedative withdrawal can require medically supervised assessment; no home detox protocol is supplied.
Withdrawal low mood is not automatically an independently qualifying induced depressive disorder.
pathways.professional_review: Current severe withdrawal/medical concerns need appropriate medical review; prescribers manage medication decisions. Depression/safety needs remain important while attribution is uncertain.

scope_gaps: Not full diagnostic/treatment modules for every alternative or all anxiety/sleep/psychotic subtypes.
ADHD, personality disorders, OCD, eating disorders and other possibilities can require review; comprehensive modules are not implemented here.
Cross-disorder clinician review, final graph, tool selection, verified instrument versions, runtime safety operations and LLM evaluation remain pending.

rules.classification_basis: DSM-5-TR 2022, separately labelled adult physical-health and condition-specific guidance

clinical_reference_rules.primary_domain_requirement: Predominant persistent depressed mood OR markedly diminished interest/pleasure in all or almost all activities.

major_depressive_like_reference.exception: Major depressive episode Criterion C regarding physiological attribution; this category still requires the medical-cause and alternative-explanation review.

descriptive_specifiers.meaning: The depressive presentation does not meet full major depressive episode criteria.
Major depressive episode criteria are met except the exclusion of a physiological medical cause (episode Criterion C); this is not an independent MDD diagnosis.
Manic/hypomanic symptoms are also present but do not predominate; professional interpretation is needed.

criteria_information_map.meaning: History, examination or laboratory evidence for a direct physiological relationship
Not better explained by another mental disorder

assessment_structure.action: Attend to current suicide-related or acute medical/cognitive concerns before ordinary assessment.
Understand what changed in mood, interest, baseline and functioning.
Identify actual reported conditions, diagnostic basis and care team; clarify suspicion versus diagnosis.
Compare physical symptoms, diagnosis, treatment changes and mood onset as separate events.
Clarify relevant symptom details already missing; review overlaps without assuming attribution.
Review past mood/activation, medication/substance effects, illness-related distress and cognitive changes.
Identify reported investigations, accessible records and remaining professional interpretation needs.
Summarize supported findings, unresolved causation, burdens, unanswered questions and actual review status.

medical_condition_reference.json.purpose: Illustrative conditions requiring clinical attribution review, not an exhaustive causal whitelist or screening checklist.

entries.assessment_relevance: Neurological course, pre-event mood and separate physical/cognitive limitations; depression after stroke is not an automatic causal diagnosis.
Reported injury/lesion and course, treatment and neurocognitive changes; no inference from lesion location by the chatbot.
Motor/non-motor course and treatment; mood symptoms may precede recognition of the motor disorder.
Reported confirmed/suspected condition, neuropsychiatric course and specialist care; do not infer disease from depression/family clues.
Actual diagnosis/testing context; overt and subclinical presentations must not be merged.
Reported endocrine diagnosis and clinician findings; do not infer it from weight change or depression.
A manual example of potential physiological association; mood symptoms do not justify a cancer diagnosis or universal cancer screening.
Medical activity, medicines and other explanations require individualized specialist review.
Possible psychiatric association; assess reported symptoms/risk context, not depression as a specific deficiency marker.
An example of association with variable causal evidence; preserve illness, treatment and psychosocial alternatives.

medical_condition_reference.json.exclusions: Common comorbidity, epidemiological association or a reported abnormal test alone does not establish direct physiological causation.

professional_review_fields.condition_identity: Clinically established condition and basis, outside patient-only verification.
professional_review_fields.literature_context: Condition-specific primary source/version, locator and evidence limitations.
professional_review_fields.competing_explanations: Independent mood illness, stress response, treatments, delirium and other conditions.
professional_review_fields.judgment_and_uncertainty: Responsible reviewer, date, supported provisional explanation and unresolved issues.

rules.classification_basis: DSM-5-TR-oriented MDD module; no silent ICD-11 criteria merge

clinical_review.scope: Adult MDD assessment and provisional explanation for professional review; not prescribing or autonomous diagnosis.

frequency_qualifiers.mood_interest: Most of day, nearly daily; breadth matters for interest/pleasure.
frequency_qualifiers.other_daily_domains: Nearly daily applies to appetite, sleep, motor, energy, guilt/worthlessness and cognition formulations.
frequency_qualifiers.exceptions: Weight has its own change/time formulation; death/suicide reports have distinct recurrent/plan/attempt formulations. Do not impose daily occurrence on all.
frequency_qualifiers.weight_example: More than 5% body-weight change over a month is a source example, not a rule for all complaints.

disorder_boundaries.meaning: Review physiological substance/medical explanations; no causal conclusion from timing alone.
At least one qualifying episode must satisfy the current psychotic-disorder exclusion.
Review lifetime mania/hypomania; preserve substance/medical exceptions and treatment context for professional interpretation.

course_review.recurrence: Separate episodes require at least two consecutive months without full MDE criteria between them; not necessarily total symptom freedom.
course_review.partial_remission: Residual symptoms without full criteria, or less than two months without significant symptoms after an episode.
course_review.full_remission: At least two months without significant signs/symptoms.
course_review.severity: Symptoms, intensity and functioning together; mild/moderate/severe cannot be inferred from one symptom or an informal count.
course_review.label_application: Current severity/psychotic coding and remission coding apply under different current-episode conditions; no billing codes are generated.

clinical_review.safety: Directly assess ideation/intent and immediate needs; use dedicated professional pathway rather than a predicted low/medium/high score.

assessment_structure.action: Check current safety concerns as indicated and invite an open account.
Clarify one current/recent period: start, end/ongoing, low mood, other symptoms and impact.
Review concurrent symptom details without combining unrelated periods or counting unknowns as absent.
If brief spells recur, review consecutive months, variability and symptoms between spells.
Review prior longer/chronic depression, activation, psychosis, relevant menstrual pattern, medical/exposure and stressor context.
Clarify only targets that remain unresolved and change interpretation; respect uncertainty/declines.
Summarize supported information and remaining classification questions; no automatic residual diagnosis.

classification_reference.json.category_definition: Predominant depressive symptoms causing clinically significant distress OR impairment, without full criteria for another depressive category or the specified adjustment presentations; clinician communicates the specific reason.

named_examples.label: Recurrent brief depression
named_examples.description: Concurrent low mood plus at least four other depressive symptoms, lasting 2–13 days, at least monthly across at least 12 consecutive months; not linked to the menstrual cycle.

requirements.recurrence: At least once per month for at least 12 consecutive months

exclusions: Lifetime presentation meeting another depressive or bipolar disorder
Current active or residual psychotic disorder

named_examples.label: Short-duration depressive-like episodes
named_examples.description: Low mood with at least four other major-episode symptom domains and clinical burden; review shorter duration, history and recurrent-brief alternative.

requirements.published_body_duration: Longer than four days and shorter than fourteen days

exclusions: Lifetime presentation meeting another depressive or bipolar disorder
Current active or residual psychotic disorder

named_examples.label: Depressive-like episode with insufficient symptoms
named_examples.description: Depressed affect plus at least one other major-episode symptom domain for at least two weeks, with clinical burden, but without full criteria for another depressive disorder.
exclusions: Lifetime presentation meeting another depressive or bipolar disorder
Current active or residual psychotic disorder

named_examples.label: Major depressive episode superimposed on specified psychotic disorders
named_examples.description: A full major depressive episode superimposed on schizophrenia, schizophreniform disorder, delusional disorder, or another specified/unspecified schizophrenia-spectrum or other psychotic disorder.
exclusions: Major depressive episode that is part of schizoaffective disorder does not merit an additional other-specified depressive diagnosis

source_issues.meaning: Published short-duration heading and body differ at exactly four days; preserve the duration and request clarification rather than choosing an automatic cutoff.

criteria_information_map.information: Long-term depressed-mood pattern and adult duration.
Associated symptom groups during depressed periods; no double counting.
Continuity and longest absence of relevant symptoms.

course_review.shared_remission_definition: The referenced shared text describes partial remission as residual symptoms below full episode requirements or less than two months without significant symptoms after an episode; full remission means no significant signs/symptoms for the past two months. source_precedence.issue: Public overview describes PDD as less severe, whereas the current classification permits a full major depressive episode throughout the persistent course.
